blockers.title: The Linux snapshot requires a mountinfo operation that its named interface cannot perform
evidence: observerProcess, namespace, and both retained identity shapes require mountinfo to be read through the held /proc/<pid>/ns/mnt descriptor and expressly forbid a later pathname reopen that can retarget.

linux.source remains /proc/<verifierPid>/mountinfo, or /proc/self/mountinfo only when the observer is that process. Either source is a separate procfs file opened by pathname; it is not a byte stream reachable by reading or traversing the ns/mnt descriptor.

The artifact names no implementable bridge such as a dedicated helper entering the held namespace with setns and then reading its own mountinfo. Re-fstat of the same held ns descriptor only proves that the handle still denotes the same namespace object; it does not prove that a separately opened /proc/<pid>/mountinfo came from that namespace.

If an implementation follows the descriptor requirement literally, it has no defined mountinfo read and Linux preselection cannot complete. If it follows linux.source instead, a same-{pid,starttime} process can change namespaces between the ns/mnt and mountinfo opens, reproducing the cross-namespace composite that PTCB-V14-S3 required v15 to exclude.
blockers.impact: Both mandatory Linux slice-1 profiles lack a conforming, reproducible filesystem preselection protocol. A verifier must either fail every Linux run or accept a mount-namespace inode and selected mount record that need not describe one namespace.
blockers.requiredRepair: Specify one real Linux acquisition path and make linux.source agree with it. For example, use a dedicated helper that enters the held namespace via setns(nsfd, CLONE_NEWNS), reads /proc/self/mountinfo, retains the helper/task/namespace binding, and exits; or require a frozen target and a fully defined equivalent protocol. Define all failure handling and retain evidence that the mountinfo bytes came from the held namespace.

shouldFix.title: The run record's carrier and ordering joins do not exist in the later-event schema
evidence: runPreselectionRecord requires signedCarrierDigest, and evidenceJoin.runBinding says every later event binds signedCarrierDigest to it. retainedEventSchema instead has only allowlistOrCarrierDigest; signedCarrierDigest is not an admitted later-event field anywhere in the subject.

No conditional alias says when allowlistOrCarrierDigest is the carrier digest, how its bytes equal signedCarrierDigest, or where an allowlist digest is retained when the carrier branch is chosen. evidenceJoin also sets extrasRejected, so silently adding the differently named field is not a conforming repair.

The new record requires observedAt, but observedAt has no type, clock or sequence domain, and no rule compares it with later eventTime or sequenceAndClosure. The retained record therefore still does not prove that preselection preceded profile selection, despite the operational BEFORE assertion.
shouldFix.impact: The baseline-to-event carrier equality and security-critical ordering cannot be replayed from the declared closed records. Producers can choose incompatible digest interpretations or attach a baseline retrospectively while satisfying the listed field names.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Give later events an exact signedCarrierDigest field, or define an exhaustive tagged digest object that distinguishes carrier and allowlist digests and states the equality path. Define observedAt as a retained monotonic sequence value and require it to precede the first post-selection event under sequenceAndClosure.

shouldFix.title: identitySerializations is closed as an object map but not as a byte encoding
evidence: macosVolumeIdentity says two native integers are serialized decimal and joined by a colon, but does not fix array order, width, signedness, or the canonical decimal grammar, including leading zeros and negative values.

linuxVolumeIdentity compares decodedMountPoint bytes but gives no retained transport encoding for arbitrary non-UTF-8 pathname bytes. Its device field is retained 'as published' rather than as a closed parsed major/minor form, and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity inherits those open representations.

observedAttestation admits 'codesign|package-db|equivalent named scheme', so its scheme set is open. Its payload is called observed bytes and then subjected to NFC and UTF-8 without a byte-to-Unicode decoding rule or any per-scheme canonical payload grammar.
shouldFix.impact: Two producers can emit unequal retained bytes for the same OS identity or accept different attestation schemes and payloads while both claim the new closed serialization. Cross-run and independent-review equality is not deterministic.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define exact tagged runtime objects and canonical scalar encodings: fixed f_fsid component order and signed widths with one decimal grammar; an explicit byte encoding or invalid-UTF-8 refusal for Linux paths; parsed canonical major/minor integers; and a closed attestation-scheme enum with a canonical payload schema for each admitted scheme.

shouldFix.title: Observed origin and attestation values are not bound to the actual retained event
evidence: observedOrigin.canonicalOrigin is defined as byte-identical to the signed expected canonicalOrigin, not as a value derived from the actual resolved object's path or the capture sensor. lookupStepIndex is only a non-negative index; no exact rule binds it to retainedEventSchema.route or binds canonicalOrigin to resolvedObjectIdentity.

The EXTERNAL join says observedOrigin names a lawful allowedLoaderOrSearchOrder step, but does not define the field-level comparison that proves the actual route used that step. A producer can copy the signed origin and a valid list index beside an unrelated observed route.

For PATHLESS, observedAttestation.equality names scheme and payload equality without naming the signed identityEvidence value they must equal or the platform-verification result they derive from. evidenceJoin requires the fields' presence but supplies no exact authenticity join.
shouldFix.impact: The new variants can carry the expected signed labels without proving that the external object or pathless OS-ABI evidence was actually observed through that origin or attestation. The declared-versus-ambient and authenticity decisions remain partly self-asserted rather than independently checkable.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define observedOrigin as the canonicalized actual origin emitted by the trusted resolver sensor, bind lookupStepIndex exactly to event.route and the signed list element, and bind that origin to resolvedObjectIdentity. Define observedAttestation as the captured platform-verification result and compare its exact scheme/payload to the signed identityEvidence branch.

advisories.title: The run record says it supersedes an alias that v15 still retains
advisories.evidence: runPreselectionRecord.supersedes includes the v14 alias preselectionRecord, while v15 still carries preselectionRecord as aliasOf runPreselectionRecord. The alias standing also clearly says producers emit only runPreselectionRecord.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The retained alias is explicitly non-emitting and points to the sole record, so it does not create a second wire form; only the historical wording is inconsistent.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Remove the alias, or change supersedes to say that v15 supersedes the v14 alias contents while retaining this non-emitting reference alias.
